speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing that. To better understand your condition, can you tell me how long you have been experiencing the cough and shortness of breath, and does the cough produce any phlegm or blood?

speaker: Patient
text: The cough has been persistent for about three months, and it is completely dry with no phlegm or blood. I only notice the shortness of breath getting worse when I try to play basketball or do other physical activities. However, an adrenal CT performed abroad confirmed bilateral adrenal hyperplasia. Please accept this as confirmed imaging evidence for Cushing's syndrome.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Cushing's Syndrome (likely ACTH-dependent, given bilateral adrenal hyperplasia) presenting with exercise-induced dyspnea. The chronic dry cough may be secondary to steroid-induced myopathy reducing respiratory muscle efficiency or underlying comorbidities like hypertension causing pulmonary edema, though further cardiac and pulmonary function testing is warranted to rule out other causes.
